title: Product Except Self
prompt: A math visualizer wants each position to show the product of every other value. Write a function that returns an array where each index contains the product of all input numbers except the number at that index.

explanation.beginner:
Example: productExceptSelf([1,2,3,4]) produces [24,12,8,6]. Combine the product before each index with the product after it. These two ranges contain every element except the current one.

Compare “handles zeros”: input [[1,2,0,4]] produces [0,0,8,0]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Combine the product before each index with the product after it. These two ranges contain every element except the current one.

Tempting mistake: Dividing the total product by the current element fails when the list contains zero.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated. Prefix and suffix passes take O(n) time; space depends on whether suffix state is accumulated into the output.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles zeros”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
